absent: Frozen page acquisition and release internals beyond the range membership check.
Bitmap sizing, allocation search, and per-bit order selection rules.
Zone, compact control, pageblock and migratetype layouts and their full lock discipline.
Compaction migrate and free scanning beyond deferral and skip-hint reset.
Page allocator free paths, buddy interaction, and highmem mapping behavior.
KASAN modes, tag propagation, page owner, table check, and architecture hooks.
Debugfs and sysfs framework error and lifetime semantics beyond call sites shown.
Device pagemap handling and memory section online state transitions.

findings.text: Provides iteration over all configured contiguous areas, invoking a caller supplied visitor with opaque data and stopping early when the visitor reports nonzero, otherwise reporting success after all areas.
Offers an overlap predicate that reports whether a caller supplied physical byte interval touches any extent belonging to the given area.
Exposes conditional return of frozen pages, succeeding only when the supplied page run lies inside a known extent of the area.
Exposes early boot carve-out from an area before activation, honoring alignment and remaining capacity limits.
Public control to clear deferral backoff after success and to raise the failed order watermark.
Translates a frame number to its descriptor only when the enclosing section and frame are online and valid, otherwise yields absence.
Finalizes freshly allocated page runs by establishing ownership metadata, sanitization interaction, and profiling hooks.
Traversal covers indices from start up to the global area tally and propagates the first nonzero visitor result unchanged.
An area extent is skipped when the query ends strictly before its start or begins at or after its end; any remaining extent implies intersection.
Reservation is refused when the handle is absent or empty, when activation already happened, when size misaligns to minimum or per-bit granularity, or when demand exceeds remaining count.
On success the first extent with enough tail room advances its early cursor and the area free tally is reduced accordingly, with the returned mapping derived from the prior cursor.
Used capacity is defined as total minus free as sampled under protection.
Largest free run is the widest clear span across all extents, scaled from bitmap units to pages by per-bit order.
Tracking records are pushed at head and popped from head, with removal skipped safely when the list is empty.
Free requests consume whole records first; a larger record is split and requeued only when per-bit order is zero, otherwise the remainder is retained and processing stops.
Debug allocation builds a tracking record before requesting pages and discards the record if page acquisition fails.
Each active area exposes controls for alloc and free plus readouts for count, granularity, used and largest chunk, with per-extent base and bitmap children and legacy links to extent zero.
Per-area read-only attributes report success and failure allocation tallies, release tally, total size and current free size.
Only activated areas receive directory entries; any creation failure unwinds previously created entries and the common root.
Failed compaction clears the attempt counter, increments backoff up to a ceiling, lowers the failed order watermark, and emits a deferral trace.
Orders below the watermark are never deferred; other orders are deferred until the attempt counter reaches an exponential bound derived from backoff.
Successful allocation clears both counter and backoff, while the watermark advances past the completed order when applicable.
Restart is indicated only when backoff is saturated and the attempt counter has reached its bound for orders at or above the watermark.
Migration scans restart from zone start and the free scan restarts from the start of the final block of the zone.
Forward search jumps to the next online section start and reverse search jumps past the prior online section end, with a build variant that never skips.
One build treats large compound pages spanning a block as persistent skip candidates, while an alternate build never reports persistence.
Reset of the skip hint requires an online page in the same zone without persistence, validated online block endpoints, and a sampled reclaimable or free page for the requested scan direction.
Isolation is always suitable when hints are ignored, otherwise it follows the absence of the block skip hint.
Translation fails for out of range sections, offline sections, invalid frames, invalid offsets within a section, and device mapped offline frames.
Software sanitizer builds never skip unpoisoning while hardware tag builds skip only on request; initialization skipping applies only under hardware tags when requested.
Allocation tagging attributes cost to the caller tag when references exist, otherwise records an early frame and marks the caller tag imprecise.
Draining converts each queued free page to allocated state before returning it and reports the highest frame seen.
Block helpers round a frame down to its containing aligned block start and up past its containing block end for a given order.
One build recognizes a sentinel order as the manual trigger path while the alternate build never reports that trigger.
One build forwards compaction events to global counters while the alternate build discards them.
Generic debug readout copies an unsigned long control value to the caller result.
Container linkage recovers the area handle from its embedded kobject wrapper.
Compaction marking establishes movable allocation state and a reference count on the supplied page.
Used and largest-chunk samplers hold the area lock in interrupt-blocking mode across counter and bitmap inspection.
All insertions and removals on the debug tracking list are serialized by the dedicated list lock.
Extent descriptor carries base frame and length plus a phase-dependent field reused as early cursor or allocation map, with an optional debug array view.
Area descriptor holds total and free tallies, per-bit order, area lock and allocation mutex, name, range count and fixed range table, flags and node, plus optional debug list and accounting.
Sysfs wrapper pairs a kernel object with a back pointer to its area.
Debug tracking node links a page run start and length into an intrusive list.
Flag enumeration distinguishes reservation on error, zone validity states, and activation.
Sysfs type binds release handling with standard operations and a fixed five attribute set covering allocation, release, total and free views.
Deferral moves from armed to deferred to reset: failures deepen backoff, checks gate retries by watermark and bound, success clears state and watermark advances.
Areas start unactivated for early cursor allocation, then become activated for bitmap allocation with debug and sysfs exposure limited to activated instances.
Debug records transition from allocated and queued to partially split and requeued or fully returned and freed, driven by write values.
Boot initialization creates the common debug root and per-area subtrees for activated areas.
Boot initialization creates the common sysfs root and per-area objects for activated areas.
Early cursor and allocation map share storage, so access must match activation phase to avoid interpreting a pointer as a frame number or vice versa.
Attempting to return part of a bitmap block when granularity exceeds one page is refused and the entry is preserved, leaving accounting unchanged.
Sysfs release frees the wrapper and clears the area back pointer, so further attribute access must not follow the stale link.
Unpoisoning precedes initialization and sanitizer handling precedes fallback tag reset, so reordering could hide corruption or fault on tagged access.
Maximum extents per area is eight.
Compaction backoff shift ceiling is six.
Huge page fragmentation check interval is five hundred milliseconds.
Compaction huge page order resolves per build to transparent huge, hugetlb, or pagetable derived order.
CMA private header uses a once-only inclusion guard.
Compaction compilation defines tracepoint creation marker.
